nodes.summary: The triple $(2, 4, 5)$ is a solution of the sum of consecutive squares problem: $0 < 3 < 4 < 5$ and $3^2 + 4^2 = 5^2$.
nodes.title: $(2, 4, 5)$ solves the sum of consecutive squares problem

nodes.summary: A triple of integers $(a, b, c)$ is a SoCS solution when $0 < a + 1 < b < c$ and $(a, b, c)$ satisfies the sum of consecutive squares equation $2\,b(b+1)(2b+1) = a(a+1)(2a+1) + c(c+1)(2c+1)$, that is, $(a+1)^2 + \dots + b^2 = (b+1)^2 + \dots + c^2$.
nodes.title: Solutions of the sum of consecutive squares problem

nodes.summary: For every integer $N > 1$, there are at most $2(N - 1)$ solutions $(a, b, c)$ of the sum of consecutive squares problem with $c - a = N$.
nodes.title: At most $2(N - 1)$ solutions with $c - a = N$

nodes.summary: There are infinitely many solutions $(a, b, c)$ of the sum of consecutive squares problem with $c - a$ even.
nodes.title: Infinitely many solutions with $c - a$ even

nodes.summary: Let $(a, b, c)$ be a solution of the sum of consecutive squares problem. Then there are infinitely many distinct integer triples $(x, y, z)$ satisfying the sum of consecutive squares equation $2\,y(y+1)(2y+1) = x(x+1)(2x+1) + z(z+1)(2z+1)$, with no order or sign condition, such that $(b - c)x + (c - a)y + (a - b)z = 0$ and $z - x \equiv c - a \pmod 2$.
nodes.title: Infinite families of solutions in a plane

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a finite set of affine planes $ux + vy + wz = t$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$, with $u, v, w, t$ real and $(u, v, w) \ne (0, 0, 0)$. Then some solution $(a, b, c)$ of the sum of consecutive squares problem lies on none of the planes in $S$, that is, $ua + vb + wc \ne t$ for every plane in $S$.
nodes.title: No finitely many planes contain all solutions

nodes.summary: For every odd integer $N \ge 3$ there is a solution $(a, b, c)$ of the sum of consecutive squares problem with $c - a = N$, together with infinitely many distinct solutions $(x, y, z)$ of that problem with $z - x$ odd, all lying in the plane $(b - c)x + (c - a)y + (a - b)z = 0$, which passes through $(a, b, c)$ and contains the line $x = y = z$.
nodes.title: Solutions with odd span $c - a$

nodes.summary: For every solution $(a, b, c)$ of the sum of consecutive squares problem, the integer $A = 3(b - c)^2\bigl(12(b - a)^2(c - b)^2 - (a - 2b + c)^4\bigr)$ is positive and is not a perfect square.
nodes.title: The Pell-type parameter is a positive nonsquare

nodes.summary: For every solution $(a, b, c)$ of the sum of consecutive squares problem, $1 < (b - a)/(c - b) < 1 + 2^{1/3} + 2^{2/3}$.
nodes.title: Bounds on the ratio of the two spans

nodes.summary: Integers $a$, $b$, $c$ satisfy the sum of consecutive squares (SoCS) equation when $2\,b(b+1)(2b+1) = a(a+1)(2a+1) + c(c+1)(2c+1)$.
nodes.title: The sum of consecutive squares equation

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
